target_customer: Adults with chronic pain paying through a subscription, later patients and insurers through a virtual clinic program
problem: Chronic pain affects about 100 million Americans and many lost at-home options as opioid prescribing tightened. Flowly offers a VR and biofeedback app as a non-drug alternative.
business_model: Consumer subscription (VR headset plus heart rate sensor), later a therapist-led virtual clinic program with insurance coverage
product_category: Digital therapeutics, VR for chronic pain

founders.name: Celine Tien
founders.background_notes: YC page: principal investigator on NIH-backed trials at UPMC and USC, director of a VR film shown at a 2017 Cannes VR event, former actor. Education not stated in sources opened.

founders.name: Narae Kim
founders.background_notes: Art and creative director across VR, film and theater per YC page.

founders.name: Julien Soros
founders.background_notes: Control algorithms on the Hyperloop One Transponics team per YC page.

competitors.name: AppliedVR
competitors.what: Clinic and hospital VR for pain and anxiety, moving to the at-home EaseVRx line for chronic back pain
competitors.traction_then: Hospital deployments; the earlier acute line ran 2015 to 2021

competitors.name: BreatheVR
competitors.what: Breathing exercise app for Gear VR and Oculus Go with a pain relief pilot

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile app plus cheap cardboard headset and a heart rate sensor streaming HR and HRV into VR scenes, with clinical trials as the harder part.

defensibility.rationale: Content and biofeedback were copyable; clinical evidence from NIH backed trials was the only real differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Flowly; AppliedVR pursued FDA authorization for a rival product.

market_need_then: The company cites 100 million Americans with chronic pain and the opioid crisis, with stricter prescribing leaving patients seeking non-drug options.

branding.domain_note: Uses flowly.world rather than a .com; the .com is used by unrelated products.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself; the name is shared with several unrelated Flowly products and the company legal name is Tamade.

pivots.from: Consumer VR and biofeedback app with $5 headset
pivots.to: Virtual clinic with licensed therapists, insurance coverage and a 14 week program
pivots.why: Not stated by a source; the current website shows the clinic model

outcome_analysis: Flowly is still operating. It started as a low cost VR and biofeedback consumer app backed by NIH funded trials, and the current site presents a therapist-led virtual clinic covered by insurers. Funding is poorly documented, so no verdict on its trajectory is supported; no shutdown or acquisition news was found.
notes: Aggregators disagree on funding: CB Insights $330K total, Bounce Watch $225K over several rounds including a $125K pre-seed in 2021-08 and a $100K grant in 2023-02, Fundediq $100K seed 2022-03. All unverified and not recorded as rounds. Education for Tien not found. Fierce Healthcare article returned 403.
